body.value: 藩制一覽表第七（結城）
藩制一覧表第七（結城）／はんせいいちらんひょう だいしち（ゆうき）

Running header (provenance), set vertically in the right-hand margin: 'Han Administration Overview Table, Fascicle 7 — Yūki.' Fascicle 7 of the Dajōkan's 1869-70 survey carries product/tax returns, religious-establishment counts, households and population. Here the parenthetical agrees with the data — every column on this leaf is Yūki's. The 覽 is printed in kyūjitai. Not data.
藩制一覧表第七（結城）
百十
百十（ひゃくじゅう）＝110

Printed book-page number in the bottom outer margin: 110. Yūki's fascicle-7 block occupies printed pages 109-111 (pdf 66-left, 67-right, 67-left); this is the middle leaf. Cross-checks against the numbering of neighbouring annotated leaves (page 6 at pdf 15-right, page 115 at pdf 69-left). Not data.
本書頁番号百十
産物稅取調帳
産物税取調帳（さんぶつぜいとりしらべちょう）

Section heading, and the first column read on the page: 'Ledger of the Investigation of Product Taxes.' It titles the extract from Yūki's own product-tax ledger that runs down its left — the two 一金 line items with their payer notes, the 〆 subtotal, and the closing declaration that everything else was untaxed. A heading, not itself a value.
産物稅取調帳
一金三十五兩也
一、金三十五両なり

First line item of the product-tax ledger: 35 ryō in gold. The warichu directly beneath names the payers — the Yūki-town pongee-and-cotton wholesalers Tahei and Chōemon. This 35 ryō plus the 3 bu of the second item makes the 〆 subtotal of 35 ryō 3 bu, which is also what the 雜稅 field reports.
一金三十五兩也
結城町紬木綿問屋　太兵衞　長右衞門
結城町 紬木綿問屋（ゆうきまち つむぎもめんどんや）太兵衛・長右衛門

Warichu (double half-column note) under the 35-ryō item, naming who paid it: the pongee-and-cotton wholesalers of Yūki town — Tahei and Chōemon. The trade description reads across two half-columns (結城町 then 紬木綿問屋); the names sit below, 太兵衞 in the right half-column and 長右衞門 in the left. Yūki-tsumugi (Yūki pongee) was the domain's signature commodity, and these two houses stood at the top of its trade. MASTER carries none of this.
結城町紬木綿問屋（納税人）
一金三步也
一、金三分なり（步＝分、一分＝四分の一両）

Second line item of the product-tax ledger: 3 bu in gold (= 0.75 ryō). 步 is the variant used here for the Edo cash sub-unit 分, and the arithmetic proves the reading: 35 ryō (item 1) + 3 bu (this item) = the printed 〆 subtotal 金三十五兩三分. Zoomed at 8x, 步 (止 over a slanted foot) is plainly a different glyph from the 分 (八 over 刀) printed in the 〆 and 雜稅 columns. Paid by the Kubota-village brokers named below. MASTER omits this line entirely.
一金三步也
久保田村紬木綿仲買人　權兵衞　半十郎　久三郎
久保田村 紬木綿仲買人（くぼたむら つむぎもめんなかがいにん）権兵衛・半十郎・久三郎

Warichu under the 3-bu item, naming its payers: the pongee-and-cotton brokers (nakagai-nin — middlemen, a rank below the wholesalers) of Kubota village — Gonbei, Hanjūrō and Kyūzaburō. The description occupies two half-columns, the three names three more, read right to left. Together with the two Yūki-town wholesalers these five men are the entire taxable trade Yūki reported, and the ranking is visible in the money: two wholesalers paid 35 ryō, three brokers paid 3 bu.
久保田村紬木綿仲買人（納税人）
〆金三十五兩三分也
〆（しめ）金三十五両三分なり

The 〆 (shime, 'total') mark closes the ledger extract: 35 ryō 3 bu = 35.75 ryō. Verified at 9x as 〆, not a numeral. Balances exactly against its two components — 35 ryō from the Yūki-town wholesalers plus 3 bu from the Kubota-village brokers — and against the 雜稅 field further left, which restates the same 35 ryō 3 bu in the survey's own form.
〆金三十五兩三分也
一蠶種白木綿其外稅無御坐候」
一、蚕種・白木綿其の外、税御座無く候（さんしゅ・しろもめん そのほか、ぜいござなくそうろう）

Absence note in the domain's own reporting voice: 'Item: on silkworm eggs, white cotton and the rest, there is no tax.' The counterpart to the two taxed items — Yūki levied only on the pongee/cotton trade at the wholesale and broker stage, and nothing on sericulture inputs or on the white cotton listed under 産物. The second glyph is 蠶 (kyūjitai for 蚕, silkworm), confirmed at 9x by the 蟲 base. The closing corner-bracket 」 ends the quoted ledger; no opening 「 is printed on this leaf.
蠶種白木綿其外稅無御坐候
雜稅　金三拾五兩三分
雑税（ざつぜい）金三十五両三分

Miscellaneous tax = 35 ryō 3 bu (35.75 ryō) — the survey field into which the whole ledger extract to its right resolves. Agrees exactly with the 〆 subtotal and with the sum of the two line items. Set against Yūki's 17,000-koku assessed holding, this is a trivial commercial levy: the domain's revenue was land, not trade.
雜稅
産物　白木綿紬縞
産物（さんぶつ）白木綿・紬縞（しろもめん・つむぎじま）

Products: white cotton cloth and striped pongee. Printed as a two-half-column note riding above the main field-label row rather than in line with it. The scan reads 縞 (shima, 'striped cloth'), not 絹 — at 9x the right-hand element is unmistakably 高. MASTER's 白木綿、紬絹 is a misread; 紬縞 also fits the domain, whose Yūki-tsumugi was woven and sold as striped goods by the very wholesalers taxed on this page.
産物
社　二百六
社（やしろ）二百六

Shrines: 206. The largest of the three religious-establishment counts on this leaf, and the one the staffing figures to its left attach to: 13 priests (神主) and 3 attendants (社人) for 206 shrines, i.e. roughly one resident officiant per thirteen. Most were unstaffed village shrines.
社
堂　三十六
堂（どう）三十六
Halls: 36. Small Buddhist chapels, counted apart from the 116 staffed temples (寺) recorded in the next column left.
堂
寺　百十六
寺（てら）百十六
Temples: 116. The facing leaf (printed page 111) supplies the clergy who staffed them — 128 monks (僧) — which works out to a little over one monk per temple.
寺
戸數　三千四百五拾貳軒
戸数（こすう）三千四百五十二軒

Households: 3,452. Against the 17,192 persons of the 人員 column this gives 4.98 persons per household. Status households are counted separately on the facing leaf (士卒 231, 穢多 60, 鉦打 4), so this is the commoner household count. The thousands digit is 千 with its ノ clearly on top — not 十.
戸數
人員　壹萬七千百九拾貳人
人員（じんいん）一万七千百九十二人

Population: 17,192. The 内 split below (男 8,682 + 女 8,337) comes to 17,019 — 173 short — and the gap is not an error: it is closed to the unit by the categories enumerated outside the sex split, namely 神主 13 + 社人 3 on this leaf and 僧 128 + 醫師 10 + 山伏 6 + 座頭 4 + 道心 8 + 修驗 1 on the facing leaf (page 111, read off the scan directly). So 人員 is the whole commoner population while the 男/女 split covers only the lay population. Two press blots sit just right of 百 and of 貳; both are ink specks with no glyph structure, and are excluded from the box.
人員
男八千六百八十貳人
男（おとこ）八千六百八十二人

Males: 8,682. Right-hand run of the 内 split, sharing its top with 女. The hundreds digit is 六 (it carries the top lid) and the tens digit is 八 (no lid, strokes splayed) — checked side by side at 7x. MASTER's 八千六百三十七人 (8,637) is a misread that reconciles with nothing, whereas 8,682 + 8,337 + the 173 specially enumerated persons = the printed total 17,192 exactly.
人員内男
女八千三百三十七人
女（おんな）八千三百三十七人

Females: 8,337. Left-hand run of the 内 split, sharing its top and bottom with 男. Both 三 register as three separate bars under row-projection and the final digit is 七, not 九. Gives a lay sex ratio of 104.1 males per 100 females. MASTER's 八千六百三十二人 (8,632) is a misread. The two runs' type physically touches at the 十/十 and 人/人 rows, so the box boundary is set at the ink-projection minimum (x764/765).
人員内女
神主拾三人
神主（かんぬし）十三人

Shinto priests: 13. Introduced by a standalone 内 ('of which') printed one column to the right at field-label height, which governs this count and the 社人 below it. These 13 are part of the 173 persons booked outside the 男/女 split of the 17,192 population.
神主
社人三人
社人（しゃにん）三人

Shrine attendants: 3. Second member of the 内 pair, printed below 神主 in the same column with a clear break between them. Thirteen priests and three attendants for the 206 shrines counted further right.
社人
